brief: J.P. Morgan's equity, FX and rates derivatives teams set out a framework for trading volatility as a separate asset class, organized around four pillars: tail and carry, relative value, beta with options, and event trading. The report mostly describes rather than argues. It sizes each market, roughly $18 trillion of SPX option open interest against $2.2 trillion in SX5E, about $20 trillion in FX options, $16 trillion of annual USD swaption volume, $400bn in listed Brent options and $250bn in GLD options, then describes the analytics used to find dislocations, namely volatility surface percentiles, implied against realized correlation, and dealer gamma, vega and delta inferred from trade-level flow. Backtested Sharpe ratios and drawdowns follow for carry and tail structures in each asset class. The live views are narrow: Mag 7 downside skew at historical lows makes mega-cap downside vega a cheap substitute for index hedges, dispersion resembles 1998-1999 because AI-driven earnings uncertainty keeps single-stock volatility high and correlation low, FX favors linear carry through options and skew selling over outright vol carry, rates favors shorting gamma in the upper right of the swaption surface and owning vega, and commodity strategists stay long-term bullish gold via call spreads.
